 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. David Bednar accepted the Yankees' free-agent qualifying offer on Nov. 17, settling their closer's position for 2027.
 As first reported by The Athletic's Tyler Kepner, Bednar will remain a mainstay in the Yanks' bullpen.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement By extending him the $23.15 million qualifying offer, the Yankees had declared their desire to retain the 32-year-old closer − a right-hander who has performed splendidly during his season-and-a-half in pinstripes.
 This is a huge raise for Bednar, who earned $9 million in 2026.
 Had he rejected the qualifying offer, Bednar would have been an unfettered free agent, and the Yanks would have received draft pick compensation if he signed elsewhere.
 Bednar's decision came as something of a surprise, with the general thinking that he'd attempt to negotiate a multi-year deal with the club (which could still happen before or after the expected Dec. 1 MLB lockout).
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Lefty-hitting second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr., 29, was not extended the QO, signaling the Yankees' intent to move on from the talented but enigmatic player.
 Why the Yankees wanted to keep David Bednar
 Since 2022, when Aroldis Chapman and Zack Britton were last in pinstripes, the Yankees have not lavished closers or high-leveraged setup relievers with big contracts.
 Yet, Bednar's steady nature and success in the Bronx - with a 2.39 ERA and 45 saves in 86 games since his arrival at the 2025 MLB trade deadline - suggests a multi-year reunion is a good possibility.
 Last week at the Las Vegas GMs meetings, Brian Cashman said that reinforcing the bullpen was "probably our biggest need" due to the free-agent status of certain 2026 Yanks relievers, led by Bednar.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Over the weekend, veteran lefty setup reliever Tim Hill and the Yankees agreed to a one-year, $2.25 million contract with a $2.5 million club option for 2028.
 Cashman acknowledged that the Yankees "dropped a big qualifying number" on Bednar, and they were "not afraid to do it" due to his track record and unflappable nature.
 "He's a cool customer," said Cashman.
 What the Yankees bullpen looks like for 2027
 Key setup reliever Paul Blackburn is also a free agent whom the Yanks would like to retain, coming off a terrific 2026 season (1.59 ERA, 62 appearances).
 The Yanks have lefty Brent Headrick under team control, as is Fernando Cruz, though the right-handed Cruz ended the 2026 season on the injured list due to a partial UCL tear.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Earlier on Monday, the Yankees claimed right-hander Chase Hampton off waivers from the Baltimore Orioles. Hampton had previously been a highly regarded starting prospect in the Yanks' system.
